PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
High risk NIPT result and abnormal ultrasound findings

SPECIMEN TYPE
Chorionic villi (uncultured)

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured chorionic villi using fluorescently labeled primers for chromosome-specific short tandem repeat (STR) markers. The test panel includes:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S391, D18S390, D18S535, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1437
- Sex chromosomes: AMELX/Y, SRY, XHPRT, DXYS218
- Quantitative marker: TAF9L (Xq21.1/3p24.2)

DNA was extracted from uncultured chorionic villi and amplified using multiplex PCR. Fragment analysis was performed on an Applied Biosystems 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak area ratios were calculated for informative markers.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: NORMAL
Two alleles detected for informative markers with normal 1:1 ratios

Chromosome 18: NORMAL
Two alleles detected for informative markers with normal 1:1 ratios

Chromosome 21: NORMAL
Two alleles detected for informative markers with normal 1:1 ratios

Sex Chromosomes: ABNORMAL
- AMELX: Single peak detected (X chromosome only)
- AMELY: Not detected
- SRY: Not detected
- XHPRT: Single allele pattern consistent with single X
- TAF9L ratio: 0.5 (consistent with single X chromosome)

CONCLUSION: 45,X - Consistent with Turner syndrome

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates a single X chromosome with absence of Y chromosome sequences. Chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 show normal disomic patterns. These findings are consistent with monosomy X (Turner syndrome), which correlates with the high-risk NIPT result and abnormal ultrasound findings reported.

The TAF9L quantitative marker ratio of 0.5 supports the presence of a single X chromosome compared to the expected ratio of 1.0 for normal female samples.

LIMITATIONS
1. This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y only
2. Mosaicism below 20% may not be reliably detected
3. Structural chromosome abnormalities, balanced rearrangements, and segmental imbalances are not detected
4. Maternal cell contamination cannot be completely excluded
5. Confined placental mosaicism may result in discordance with fetal karyotype

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis from cultured chorionic villi is recommended to:
- Confirm the 45,X finding
- Exclude low-level mosaicism
- Detect any structural abnormalities not identified by QF-PCR
- Provide comprehensive cytogenetic evaluation

Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss the implications of Turner syndrome, including associated medical conditions and management options.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
